newsitem.title: USA: Equitable of Iowa had not been seeking buyer.
newsitem.headline: Equitable of Iowa had not been seeking buyer.

text.p: Equitable of Iowa Cos, which has agreed to be acquired by Dutch financial company ING Groep NV for $68 a share, said that prior to this deal the company had no plans to sell itself.

"However, as we learned more about ING we realized that this was a unique opportunity to provide our shareholders with a price consideration consistent with the long-term superior performance of our business while strengthening our operations so that we could continue to deliver strong results," Fred Hubbell, chairman, president and chief executive officer, said in a statement.

Equitable of Iowa said its board approved a definitive merger agreement to become a wholly owned subsidiary of ING for $2.2 billion plus assumption of debt. ING will pay $68 per Equitable share of common stock and assume about $400 million in debt.
The merger is expected to close by the end of 1997, subject to customary conditions including regulatory and Equitable of Iowa shareholder approval.
The transaction will be tax free for Equitable shareholders to the extent they exchange their shares for American Depository Shares of ING.

Total cash elections by Equitable shareholders will be limited to 50 percent of the aggregate consideration, while stock elections will be limited to 60 percent. The exchange ratio for ING depository shares will be determined by dividing $68 by an average trading price of the ING depository shares prior to closing.

The merger of Equitable of Iowa with the existing ING life insurance business in North America will double ING's life insurance assets under management in the United States to more than $20 billion, the company said.

Equitable of Iowa will retain its name and corporate autonomy and will be part of the ING Financial Services International North America divisions, which includes Life of Georgia, Security Life of Denver, The Southland Group and The Netherlands Insurance Co.
"Equitable of Iowa brings to this partnership a highly successful, growth oriented annuity and life insurance company," Hubbell said. "We will significantly ramp up ING's U.S. insurance presence."

"Equitable of Iowa will play a significant role for us in the U.S. market," ING Chairman of the Executive Board Aad Jacobs said in a statement. "This acquisition will enhance our competitive position, lifting our U.S. total premium level ranking to 21st, from its current 41st position."

As part of the acquisition, Hubbell will join the ING FSI North American general management team as president and chief executive officer of the expanded U.S. retail life and annuity businesses. He will report to Glenn Hilliard, chairman and chief executive officer of FSI North America.
In addition, Equitable of Iowa board members will be invited to join the ING North America Insurance board.
